# CartPilot — Make the cart agent faster + fix what the logs show

## Context
After PR #6 the agent is accurate and no longer blocked, but the user wants it faster, and an overall review of what worked and what didn't. Evidence comes from the TinyFish step logs of the user's post-fix build (`eea471bb`, 5 items, 41 steps, 450s) and my test run (`0955d743`, 3 items, 19 steps, 164s).

### Where the time goes (step logs; ~10s per agent step)
| Cost | Evidence | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| ~36s browser start + **~60s on the home page** (load 26s, popups 32s) | first 2 steps | Start directly on the first item's search-results URL |
| **4–5 steps per item through the search box**: open → type → wait → "go to full results", because typing only shows a suggestion dropdown | every item; eggs took 3 tries and 2 product-page visits (~3 min) | Open `…/eng/search.html?query=<q>` directly. This URL was never blocked; only product pages were. Never open product pages. |
| **Hit the 7-minute cap** → chicken/pork left at 1 pack instead of 2; garlic falsely reported "unavailable" ("budget exhausted") | result notes | Fewer steps per item, a slightly longer cap, and a separate `not_reached` outcome that is retried |
| 2–3 steps (~30s) opening the cart to read a subtotal T&T shows as $0.00 | end of both runs | Drop the cart check. The cart URL is fixed (`/eng/cart`). |
| One agent at a time, plus ~36s browser start per run | runs are sequential | Measure 2 agents at once now that deep links are gone (see 4) |

**Target:** about 3 steps per item (open search URL, add, +/−) instead of 6–9, so an 8-item cart takes about 3–4 minutes instead of 7–10, at about half the cost.

## Changes

### 1. Faster agent goal (`server/cart/buildCart.js`)
- `runBatch` starts at `searchUrlFor(batch[0].searchQuery)` instead of the home page.
- **Goal per item:**
  - "Go to this exact URL: `<search URL>`";
  - find the card named exactly `<product>`, scrolling the results if needed;
  - use the card's add/+ control to reach the quantity;
  - **never open product pages, never use the search box or its suggestion dropdown**.
  
  The "if no card matches, unavailable" rule only applies **after the results have loaded and been scrolled**.
- **Remove** the end-of-run cart check and `cart_subtotal`. Keep `cart_url` defaulting to `https://www.tntsupermarket.com/eng/cart`. Drop subtotal parsing and the UI line.
- **New outcome `not_reached`:** "If you are running out of time, stop and report items you didn't finish as `not_reached`."
- **Weight items:** "press + (N−1) times after adding". The note stays as it is.
- **Time cap:** `durationFor(n) = min(540, 90 + 60·n)` (TinyFish runs end at 10 minutes).
- **Items per run:** stays at 5. Fewer runs mean fewer ~36s browser starts.

### 2. Retry what wasn't finished
- Items reported `not_reached`, plus items missing from a run that ended on the time cap (FAILED/timeout), are retried in the same single follow-up pass as `blocked` items. The pass stays at one retry, with no pause unless something was blocked.
- Final outcome after the retry: `not_reached` → `failed` with the note "The agent ran out of time on this item."

### 3. Live activity feed: the build feels faster and is easier to debug
- While polling, store the latest step's action on the run (`run.lastAction`, e.g. "Add first unit of chicken thigh to cart"). `getRun` already returns `steps[]`, and polling already passes `screenshots=none&html=none`.
- `CartBuild.jsx` shows "Agent: <latest action>" under each live view, plus the elapsed time and step count (≈ cost at $0.016/step).

### 4. Measure parallelism instead of guessing
- Make concurrency a setting: `CART_AGENT_CONCURRENCY`, default **1**. `runCartBuild` keeps up to N batches running at once, with the same polling loop. Batches are split evenly (e.g. 8 items → 4 + 4 when N = 2).
- **Live A/B on the same 6 items:** N = 1 vs N = 2, both using the new search-URL goal (about 4 runs, ~$1, may add test items to the T&T cart, never checks out).
  - N = 2 with **no Access Denied** → default 2 (halves the wall time).
  - Any block → keep 1 and write the result in the README.

### 5. Other improvements found in the logs (small, included)
- **Old build records** (from before PR #6) have no `attempt`/`searchQuery`, so the UI shows "aundefined" and "q=undefined". Default these when reading.
- **Planner search terms** are sometimes oddly cased ("Chicken thigh Boneless"): lowercase them in `consolidate.js` (already done for new plans; also lowercase in `planCartRun`).
- **The run's log link** (`agent.tinyfish.ai/runs/<id>`) is already shown; keep it.

### Out of scope (recorded in the README as future ideas)
- Adding items through T&T's own cart API from inside a TinyFish browser session. That would be much faster, but it bypasses the agent the TinyFish track is judged on and needs the user's T&T session token.
- Starting the next run's browser early to hide the ~36s start.

## Tests
- **Goal:** starts on the search URL; contains each item's search URL, the "never open product pages / search box" rule, `not_reached`, and no cart-check step.
- **Retry:** `not_reached` and time-cap items are retried once, then end `failed` with the time note.
- **Concurrency:** with N = 2, at most 2 runs at once, batches split evenly; N = 1 behaves as before.
- **Activity feed:** `lastAction` is saved from the poll results.
- **UI:** old records without `attempt`/`searchQuery` render without "undefined".
- The existing 73 tests keep passing (updating assertions for the start URL and the removed subtotal).

## Verification
1. Run `npm test`; all pass.
2. **Live:** the 6-item A/B from section 4. Record the wall time, steps, outcomes and any blocks for N = 1 and N = 2, then pick the default.
3. **Browser:** Approve → the live view shows the agent's current action → Stop still works.
4. Update the README (timings table, lessons). Commit to `phase-6c-faster-agent`, stacked on #6, and open a PR with the before/after numbers.

## Context
The user's real build (task `54c344a3`, 9 items) mostly failed and took about 20 minutes. There was also no way to stop the agents from CartPilot; the user had to cancel one in the TinyFish dashboard.

### What actually happened (TinyFish run records + local database)
| Run | Items | Result | Time / steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| a7fccc49 | eggs, chicken thighs, flank steak, ground pork | every product page **"Access Denied"** → 3 failed, eggs **mis-reported as out_of_stock** | 15 min / **116 steps** |
| 26f876d8 | bok choy, broccoli, garlic, green onion | bok choy + green onion "Access Denied"; broccoli/garlic were already in the cart | 12.5 min / **106 steps** |
| c5e05007 | firm tofu | cancelled by the user in the dashboard | 0 steps |

### Root causes
1. **T&T's edge blocked the agent.** "Access Denied" is an IP/fingerprint block. TinyFish's anti-bot guide says: use the **stealth** browser with a proxy, and **"start at the front door — direct deep links look robotic"**. We used the default (lite) browser, opened **product deep links**, and ran **2 agents at once on the same account**. 2. **No fail-fast.** The goal only said to stop on a CAPTCHA, so on "Access Denied" each agent kept retrying and searching for 100+ steps. That's about $1.70 and 12–15 minutes per agent for nothing.
3. **Mislabelled outcomes.** There's no "blocked" status, so a block became `out_of_stock`, `unavailable` or `failed`.
4. **Items sold by weight.** T&T's cart counts these in pounds (broccoli showed 1.5), so the "quantity mismatch" warning for them was a false alarm.
5. **No cancel.** CartPilot can't stop runs. A server restart also leaves orphaned TinyFish runs still costing money (cancelling is idempotent: `POST /v1/runs/{id}/cancel`).

## Changes

### 1. Agent strategy (`server/cart/buildCart.js`, `server/cart/agent.js`)
- **Stealth browser:** `startRun` sends `browser_profile: "stealth"`, keeping `proxy_config` CA, `use_profile` and `profile_id`.
- **Front door instead of deep links:**
  - Each run starts at `https://www.tntsupermarket.com/eng/`.
  - For each item the agent opens the **T&T search** for that item's research query (already stored as `research.items[i].query`; pass it as `searchQuery` through `planCartRun`).
  - It finds the card whose name **exactly matches** the product name, then uses that card's add / + control to reach the quantity.
  - Only if the search card has no add button does it click into the product page.

- **Fail fast:** add `"blocked"` to the item status enum. Goal rule: "If any page shows Access Denied / 403 / a robot check, **stop immediately**: mark that item and all remaining items `blocked`, then finish."
- **Pacing:**
  - **one agent at a time** (`MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS = 1`), so two sessions never share the account;
  - **≤5 items per run**;
  - `max_duration_seconds = 120 + 60 × items` (≤ 420), so a stuck run can't burn 15 minutes.

- **Outcome mapping:** a `blocked` outcome gets its own count. `cartRun.status` stays `built` / `partial` / `failed`, plus `cancelled`.
- **Weight items:** `planCartRun` keeps `perLb` per item. The goal says "sold by weight: add N pack(s); the cart may show pounds (e.g. 1.5), that's fine". The mismatch note is skipped for weight items.

### 2. Cancel (`server/cart/buildCart.js`, `server/app.js`, `server/index.js`, UI)
- `agent.cancelRun(id)` → `POST /v1/runs/{id}/cancel`.
- `runCartBuild` takes a `signal` (AbortController). On abort it:
  - stops starting batches;
  - calls `cancelRun` on active runs;
  - marks items still `pending` as `cancelled` ("Stopped before this item");
  - keeps the outcomes of finished items;
  - finishes with `cartRun.status = "cancelled"` and the task `built` (items already added stay in the T&T cart, and the user can rebuild).

- **New route:** `POST /api/shopping-tasks/:id/build-cart/cancel` (scope `read:profile`: stopping is always safe and must never need a consent popup). 404 for other users' tasks, 409 if not building, 202 otherwise.
- **Restart:** `openDb` records the run IDs of builds interrupted by a restart (`db.interruptedRunIds`). `server/index.js` cancels them through the agent on startup, so no orphaned runs keep costing money.
- **UI** (`src/CartBuild.jsx`):
  - a **Stop agent** button while building, with the note "Items already added stay in your T&T cart";
  - after a click it reads "Stopping…";
  - `cancelled` / `blocked` chips;
  - a clear summary for a cancelled or blocked build.
- **Wording:** the blocked state says what to do: "T&T blocked the agent. Wait a few minutes and rebuild, or add these on T&T."

### 3. Tests
- **Cart builder:**
  - goal starts at the front door, uses search queries, and includes the stop-on-Access-Denied rule;
  - one run at a time; ≤5 items per run;
  - blocked items are retried once in a new run, then labelled `blocked`;

  - weight items get no mismatch note;
  - stealth is passed through.
- **API:** cancel route (202 / 404 for other users / 409 when not building / ends `cancelled`); interrupted run IDs exposed after a restart.

1. Run `npm test`; all pass.
2. **Live** (adds a few cheap items to the user's T&T cart, never checks out; they're OK'd for test items):
   - (a) A 3-item build that includes two items that were blocked before (green onion, ground pork). Check the outcomes, time (aim under 5 minutes) and step count, then do a read-only cart check.
   - (b) Start a build and **cancel** it through the new path; confirm TinyFish shows the run `CANCELLED` and pending items are marked cancelled.

| **Hit the 7-minute cap** → chicken/pork left at 1 pack instead of 2; garlic falsely reported "unavailable" ("budget exhausted") | result notes | Fewer steps per item, a slightly longer cap, and a separate `not_reached` outcome that is retried |

| One agent at a time, plus ~36s browser start per run | runs are sequential | Measure 2 agents at once now that deep links are gone (see 4) |

**Target:** about 3 steps per item (open search URL, add, +/−) instead of 6–9, so an 8-item cart takes about 3–4 minutes instead of 7–10, at about half the cost.

## Changes

### 1. Faster agent goal (`server/cart/buildCart.js`)
- `runBatch` starts at `searchUrlFor(batch[0].searchQuery)` instead of the home page.
- **Goal per item:**
  - "Go to this exact URL: `<search URL>`";
  - find the card named exactly `<product>`, scrolling the results if needed;
  - use the card's add/+ control to reach the quantity;
  - **never open product pages, never use the search box or its suggestion dropdown**.
  
  The "if no card matches, unavailable" rule only applies **after the results have loaded and been scrolled**.
- **Remove** the end-of-run cart check and `cart_subtotal`. Keep `cart_url` defaulting to `https://www.tntsupermarket.com/eng/cart`. Drop subtotal parsing and the UI line.
- **New outcome `not_reached`:** "If you are running out of time, stop and report items you didn't finish as `not_reached`."
- **Weight items:** "press + (N−1) times after adding". The note stays as it is.
- **Time cap:** `durationFor(n) = min(540, 90 + 60·n)` (TinyFish runs end at 10 minutes).
- **Items per run:** stays at 5. Fewer runs mean fewer ~36s browser starts.

### 2. Retry what wasn't finished
- Items reported `not_reached`, plus items missing from a run that ended on the time cap (FAILED/timeout), are retried in the same single follow-up pass as `blocked` items. The pass stays at one retry, with no pause unless something was blocked.
- Final outcome after the retry: `not_reached` → `failed` with the note "The agent ran out of time on this item."

### 3. Live activity feed: the build feels faster and is easier to debug
- While polling, store the latest step's action on the run (`run.lastAction`, e.g. "Add first unit of chicken thigh to cart"). `getRun` already returns `steps[]`, and polling already passes `screenshots=none&html=none`.
- `CartBuild.jsx` shows "Agent: <latest action>" under each live view, plus the elapsed time and step count (≈ cost at $0.016/step).

### 4. Measure parallelism instead of guessing
- Make concurrency a setting: `CART_AGENT_CONCURRENCY`, default **1**. `runCartBuild` keeps up to N batches running at once, with the same polling loop. Batches are split evenly (e.g. 8 items → 4 + 4 when N = 2).
- **Live A/B on the same 6 items:** N = 1 vs N = 2, both using the new search-URL goal (about 4 runs, ~$1, may add test items to the T&T cart, never checks out).
  - N = 2 with **no Access Denied** → default 2 (halves the wall time).
  - Any block → keep 1 and write the result in the README.

### 5. Other improvements found in the logs (small, included)
- **Old build records** (from before PR #6) have no `attempt`/`searchQuery`, so the UI shows "aundefined" and "q=undefined". Default these when reading.
- **Planner search terms** are sometimes oddly cased ("Chicken thigh Boneless"): lowercase them in `consolidate.js` (already done for new plans; also lowercase in `planCartRun`).
- **The run's log link** (`agent.tinyfish.ai/runs/<id>`) is already shown; keep it.

### Out of scope (recorded in the README as future ideas)
- Adding items through T&T's own cart API from inside a TinyFish browser session. That would be much faster, but it bypasses the agent the TinyFish track is judged on and needs the user's T&T session token.
- Starting the next run's browser early to hide the ~36s start.

- **Goal:** starts on the search URL; contains each item's search URL, the "never open product pages / search box" rule, `not_reached`, and no cart-check step.
- **Retry:** `not_reached` and time-cap items are retried once, then end `failed` with the time note.
- **Concurrency:** with N = 2, at most 2 runs at once, batches split evenly; N = 1 behaves as before.
- **Activity feed:** `lastAction` is saved from the poll results.
- **UI:** old records without `attempt`/`searchQuery` render without "undefined".
- The existing 73 tests keep passing (updating assertions for the start URL and the removed subtotal).

## Verification
1. Run `npm test`; all pass.
2. **Live:** the 6-item A/B from section 4. Record the wall time, steps, outcomes and any blocks for N = 1 and N = 2, then pick the default.
3. **Browser:** Approve → the live view shows the agent's current action → Stop still works.
4. Update the README (timings table, lessons). Commit to `phase-6c-faster-agent`, stacked on #6, and open a PR with the before/after numbers.

lines: 3. **Plan.** Google Gemini (structured JSON output) produces a structured meal plan and ingredient list. Server code (not the LLM) merges duplicates, removes pantry items and exclusions.

4. **Research.** TinyFish Fetch reads T&T's search page for every item at once (about 30–40s for a full list). Server code parses the results, screens out allergens and "different foods" (quail eggs aren't eggs), picks the cheapest pack that covers the recipe quantity, retries simpler searches when nothing matches, and totals the cart against the budget.

5. **Review.** You swap to another product, change pack counts, remove or restore items, or search T&T again with your own words. The total updates instantly and is re-computed by the server (it never trusts prices from the browser). Warnings name the biggest lines when you're over budget.

-6. **Approve & build cart.** Approving asks Auth0 for the `build:cart` permission at that moment (consent popup the first time). The server checks the permission and that the total and item count match what you approved, records the approval, then starts a TinyFish browser agent signed in to T&T (stealth browser, one agent at a time, up to 5 items per run). Like a shopper, it starts on T&T's home page, searches for each item, and sets the matching product's cart quantity to exactly what you chose. You can watch it live and **stop it** at any time (items already added stay in your cart). If T&T's website blocks the agent ("Access Denied"), it stops right away instead of burning time, and those items are retried once in a fresh session. Each item reports added / quantity set / out of stock / blocked / stopped, and the agent is told never to check out or pay; you finish on T&T.

+6. **Approve & build cart.** Approving asks Auth0 for the `build:cart` permission at that moment (consent popup the first time). The server checks the permission and that the total and item count match what you approved, records the approval, then starts TinyFish browser agents signed in to T&T (stealth browser, two at a time, up to 5 items each). Each agent goes straight to T&T's search results page for an item and sets the matching product's cart quantity to exactly what you chose (for items sold by weight, a target in pounds). A live feed shows what each agent is doing, how long it has taken and how many steps (≈ cost) it has used. You can watch it live and **stop it** at any time (items already added stay in your cart). If T&T's website blocks an agent ("Access Denied"), it stops right away instead of burning time; blocked items, and items an agent ran out of time on or couldn't load, are retried once in a fresh session (one agent at a time after a block). Each item reports added / quantity set / out of stock / blocked / stopped, and the agent is told never to check out or pay; you finish on T&T.

- T&T's website answers "Access Denied" to automated **direct product-page links** and to **two agents on one account at once**, while its search pages keep working. The agent therefore uses TinyFish's stealth browser, starts at the home page, adds items from search results, and runs one at a time. On the same items this went from ~27 minutes / 222 steps with mostly failures to ~3 minutes / 19 steps with everything added.

+- Going straight to `search.html?query=…` instead of typing in the search box cut each item from 4–9 agent steps to 2–3 (the box only shows a suggestion dropdown first). The best runs add an item in ~30s.

-- T&T's cart counts weight items in pounds (e.g. 1.5), so those aren't flagged as quantity mismatches.
- If the server restarts mid-build, leftover TinyFish runs are cancelled on startup so they don't keep costing money.

gh pr create --base phase-6b-cart-agent-fixes --head phase-6c-faster-agent --title "Speed up the cart agent and fix issues found in its logs" --body-file - <<'EOF'
> Stacked on #6. Merge #6 first; then this PR should retarget to `main` (if not, change its base to `main`).

## What the TinyFish step logs showed
Agent steps take **8–35s each**, so the number of steps decides the speed. In the post-#6 build (5 items, 41 steps, 7.5 min):
- **Browser start and the home page:** ~35s to start the browser, then ~60s on the home page and popups.
- **The search box:** 4–5 steps per item. Typing only opens a suggestion dropdown, so the agent has to go on to the full results. Eggs alone took ~3 minutes.
- **The time cap:** the run hit its 7-minute limit, so 2 weight items got only 1 pack, and garlic was **falsely reported "unavailable"** because the agent had run out of time.
- **The cart check:** ~30s at the end to read a subtotal T&T shows as $0.00.

## Changes
- **Straight to the search results:** each item opens `search.html?query=…` directly. No search box, no product pages (those were the blocked ones), no cart check at the end. **2–3 steps per item.**
- **Two agents at once by default**, with items split evenly. In live tests with search pages T&T didn't block this, and it hides one slow session behind a fast one.
  - The retry pass **drops to one agent after any block**.
  - `CART_AGENT_CONCURRENCY=1` forces one agent at a time.
- **`not_reached` outcome:** used when time runs out, or when a page won't load after one reload (~15s). These items are retried once in a fresh session instead of being called "unavailable". After that, they show "ran out of time".
- **Subscription popup:** explicit instruction to close it (it cost ~100s in one run).
- **Weight items get a pound target** (e.g. "about 2 lb") and are never reduced. Before, the agent cut 2 lb of pork down to "1".
- **Live activity feed in the UI:** each agent's current action ("Navigate to ground pork search results"), elapsed time, steps and approximate cost.
- **Wording:** "Not at your store", with advice to pick another option or choose a substitute.
- **Time cap:** 90s + 60s per item (max 9 min).

## Live results (real T&T account)
| Version | Items | Wall | Steps | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original (product links, 2 agents) | 9 | ~20 min | 222 | Mostly "Access Denied" |
| #6 (home page + search box, 1 agent) | 5 | 7.5 min | 41 | 1 false "unavailable" |
| Search URLs, 1 agent | 6 | 6.6 min | 25 | All handled; 2 not stocked at the store |

content.text:
Yes, it can go faster, though there's a ceiling. I went through the TinyFish step logs, made the changes, and tested them on your T&T account. Everything is in **PR #7: https://github.com/GLeanM/HackWestern13/pull/7**, which builds on #6. All 76 tests pass.

## How fast it is now (live, on your T&T account)
| Version | Items | Time | Agent steps | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original | 9 | ~20 min | 222 | Mostly "Access Denied" |
| After the Stop button fix (#6), your build | 5 | 7.5 min | 41 | Hit the time limit; garlic falsely "unavailable" |
| **New: straight to search results, 1 agent** | 6 | 6.6 min | **25** | All handled correctly |
| **New: 2 agents + retry** | 4 | 5.6 min | **20** | All added, weight amounts correct |

At its best, an agent now adds an item in about **30 seconds (2–3 steps)**, compared with 6–9 steps before. Fewer steps also means it costs less.

## What I changed
- **Straight to T&T's search results** for each item. The search box was costing 4–5 steps per item, because typing only shows a suggestion list first. It also skips the end-of-run cart check, since T&T shows $0.00 there anyway.
- **Two agents at once by default.** With the new approach T&T didn't block it, and a fast agent makes up for a slow one. If T&T ever blocks, the retry runs with one agent. Setting `CART_AGENT_CONCURRENCY=1` forces one agent.
- **Out of time no longer means "unavailable".** Items an agent didn't get to, or whose page wouldn't load, are marked separately and retried in a fresh session. The retry fixed a stuck firm-tofu page in 2 of 3 tests.
- **Popups:** the agent is told how to close T&T's subscription popup. That popup cost about 100 seconds in one run.
- **Weight items:** the agent gets a target in pounds ("about 2 lb") and never reduces an existing amount. Before, it had cut 2 lb of pork down to "1".
- **Live activity feed:** the build screen shows what each agent is doing ("Navigate to ground pork search results"), elapsed time, steps and approximate cost.

## What worked, what didn't, and what could be better
**Worked well:**
- the Stop button, and blocks being reported clearly;
- setting the exact quantity, including "set tofu from 2 to 1";
- retries in a fresh session;
- the Auth0 approval flow;
- the price search, which rarely failed.

**Didn't work, now fixed:**
- opening product pages directly (blocked by T&T);
- the search box (slow);
- weight quantities;
- items mislabelled "unavailable".

**Still to improve:**
1. **Items your store doesn't stock.** CartPilot reads prices from T&T's main online store, but your N6G store doesn't stock everything. Burnbrae Large Eggs (12pcs) was missing in both tests. These now show "Not at your store", but ideally they'd be caught on the review screen. Pricing from your own store is the biggest remaining gap in accuracy.
2. **Inconsistent agents.** The same agent found garlic in one run and missed it in another, on a page with 35 results. The retry usually catches it.
3. **Time outside CartPilot's control:** about 35 seconds for TinyFish to start each browser, 8–35 seconds per step depending on the session, and slow T&T pages. Realistically **5–6 minutes for an 8-item cart**.
4. **To get down to seconds,** you'd have to add items through T&T's own cart system inside the TinyFish browser. That would bypass the browsing agent the TinyFish track judges, so I've only listed it as a future idea in the README.

## Next steps for you
- **Merge #6, then #7.** If #7 doesn't switch to `main` automatically, change its base to `main`.
- **Restart `npm run dev`** and try a build. Watch the activity feed, then tick the manual check on PR #7.
- **Your T&T cart has test items from today:** green onion, tofu, garlic, ground pork (~2 lb), chicken thigh (2.5 lb), broccoli and eggs. Clear them before a real checkout or the demo. Nothing was ever checked out.
- **Today's TinyFish usage:** my live tests used about 120 agent steps in total (roughly $2).

      "text": "> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.tinyfish.ai/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
# TinyBrowser API Reference
> Complete reference for the TinyBrowser endpoints
## Endpoints
| Method | Path | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `POST` | `https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai` | Create a browser session |
| `DELETE` | `https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai/{session\_id}` | Terminate a browser session |
All requests require an `X-API-Key` header. See [Authentication](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/authentication.md).
> [!NOTE]
>
> The SDKs (`tinyfish` for Python and `@tiny-fish/sdk` for TypeScript) target `https://agent.tinyfish.ai/v1/browser` by default, while the REST host documented here is `https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai`. Both hosts are supported and behave identically.
> [!NOTE]
>
> Session creation typically takes 10-30 seconds. Set your HTTP client timeout to at least 60 seconds. Direct TinyBrowser sessions are isolated; use [TinyProfiles](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/tinyagent/api/profiles/tinyprofile.md) when you need reusable cookies or storage.
\*\*\*
## Request
```json theme={null}
{
"url": "https://www.tinyfish.ai",
"timeout\_seconds": 300,
"proxy\_config": { "country\_code": "DE" }
}
```
### Parameters
\*\*url\*\* `string`
Target URL the session will navigate to on startup. Bare domains (e.g. `tinyfish.ai`) are automatically prefixed with `https://`. Omit to start at `about:blank`.
\*\*timeout\\_seconds\*\* `integer`
Inactivity timeout in seconds (5–86400). Defaults to your account's maximum.
\*\*proxy\\_config\*\* `object`
How the session connects to the internet. Omit to use the TinyFish residential proxy in the US.
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Set `false` to connect directly, with no proxy. Other fields are ignored. |
| `type` | `"tinyfish"` \| `"custom"` | `"tinyfish"` | `tinyfish` uses the TinyFish residential proxy. `custom` routes through your own proxy. |
| `country\_code` | `string` | `"US"` | Exit country for the `tinyfish` proxy. Any [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO\_3166-1\_alpha-2) code, case-insensitive (e.g. `DE`, `jp`). Not allowed with `custom`. |
| `url` | `string` | — | Your proxy URL. Required with `custom`. Must be `http://` or `https://`. |
| `username` | `string` | — | Username for your custom proxy. |
| `password` | `string` | — | Password for your custom proxy. |
Unknown fields are rejected with `400`.
### Proxy Behavior
\* \*\*Sticky exit IP.\*\* With the `tinyfish` proxy, a session keeps the same exit IP across all its connections, including after idle periods. Different sessions get different IPs. Residential IPs can occasionally go offline; the session then moves to a new IP in the same country.
\* \*\*Default.\*\* Sessions created without `proxy\_config` use the `tinyfish` proxy in the US.
\* \*\*Custom proxies.\*\* TinyFish connects to your proxy as given and does not rotate or pin its IP. Only `http://` and `https://` proxies are supported.
\*\*\*
## Response
On success, returns `201 Created` with a JSON body containing `session\_id`, `cdp\_url`, and `base\_url`.
```json theme={null}
{
"session\_id": "br-a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
"cdp\_url": "wss://example.tinyfish.io/cdp",
"base\_url": "https://example.tinyfish.io"
}
```
\*\*session\\_id\*\* `string`
Unique identifier for this session.
\*\*cdp\\_url\*\* `string`
WebSocket URL for browser connection. Pass this to Playwright's `connect\_over\_cdp` or any CDP client.
\*\*base\\_url\*\* `string`
HTTPS base URL for the session. Use to access session endpoints such as `/pages`.
\*\*\*
## DELETE — Terminate a Session
```bash theme={null}
DELETE https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai/{session\_id}
```
Terminates the session immediately. If the session is already ended this call is a no-op and still returns `204`.
### Path Parameters
\*\*session\\_id\*\* `string` \*required\*
The `session\_id` returned when the session was created.
### Response
Returns `204 No Content` with an empty body on success.
### Error Codes
| HTTP Status | Error Code | Cause |
| - | - | - |
| 400 | `INVALID\_INPUT` | `session\_id` is missing or empty. |
| 401 | `MISSING\_API\_KEY` / `INVALID\_API\_KEY` | Missing or invalid `X-API-Key`. |
| 404 | `NOT\_FOUND` | Session does not exist or belongs to a different API key. |
| 409 | `RETRY\_REQUIRED` | Conflicting operation on the session. Termination not confirmed — retry the delete shortly. |
| 429 | `RATE\_LIMIT\_EXCEEDED` | Browser infrastructure rate limit. Honor `Retry-After`. |
| 500 | `INTERNAL\_ERROR` | Unexpected or non-retryable infrastructure failure. Termination is not confirmed — the session may still be running; retry the delete. |
| 503 | `SERVICE\_BUSY` | Browser infrastructure temporarily unavailable. Termination not confirmed — retry, honoring `Retry-After`. |
| 504 | `TIMEOUT` | Browser infrastructure timed out terminating the session. Retry. |
Infrastructure errors include `error.details.upstream\_status` — the backend status when one was received, otherwise the status TinyFish synthesized (502 for transport failures, 504 for timeouts). Every error also carries `request\_id`, echoed in the `X-Request-ID` header; quote it when contacting support.
\*\*\*
## Debugging — Open DevTools Inspector
Poll `GET {base\_url}/pages` and open the `devtoolsFrontendUrl` of the first non-blank page to inspect the live browser session.
```python Python theme={null}
async def get\_inspector\_url(base\_url: str) -> str:
async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
for \_ in range(20):
pages = (await client.get(f"{base\_url}/pages", timeout=5)).json()
nav = next((p for p in pages if p.get("url") not in ("", "about:blank", "about:newtab")), None)
if nav:
return nav["devtoolsFrontendUrl"]
await asyncio.sleep(1)
raise TimeoutError("navigation never completed")
```
```typescript TypeScript theme={null}
async function getInspectorUrl(baseUrl: string): Promise {
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/pages`);
```

## Endpoints
| Method | Path | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `POST` | `https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai` | Create a browser session |

\*\*\*
## Request
```json theme={null}
{
"url": "https://www.tinyfish.ai",
"timeout\_seconds": 300,
"proxy\_config": { "country\_code": "DE" }
}
```

### Parameters
\*\*url\*\* `string`
Target URL the session will navigate to on startup. Bare domains (e.g. `tinyfish.ai`) are automatically prefixed with `https://`. Omit to start at `about:blank`.
\*\*timeout\\_seconds\*\* `integer`
Inactivity timeout in seconds (5–86400). Defaults to your account's maximum.
\*\*proxy\\_config\*\* `object`
How the session connects to the internet. Omit to use the TinyFish residential proxy in the US.
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Set `false` to connect directly, with no proxy. Other fields are ignored. |
| `type` | `"tinyfish"` \| `"custom"` | `"tinyfish"` | `tinyfish` uses the TinyFish residential proxy. `custom` routes through your own proxy. |

| `url` | `string` | — | Your proxy URL. Required with `custom`. Must be `http://` or `https://`. |
| `username` | `string` | — | Username for your custom proxy. |
| `password` | `string` | — | Password for your custom proxy. |
Unknown fields are rejected with `400`.
### Proxy Behavior
\* \*\*Sticky exit IP.\*\* With the `tinyfish` proxy, a session keeps the same exit IP across all its connections, including after idle periods. Different sessions get different IPs. Residential IPs can occasionally go offline; the session then moves to a new IP in the same country.

```bash theme={null}
DELETE https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai/{session\_id}
```

# About TinyProfile
> Create, set up, and use TinyProfiles from the TinyAgent API
Use the TinyProfiles API to create persistent browser state, set it up once, and reuse it in future
TinyAgent API runs. The happy path is simple: create a profile, save a logged-in setup session, then pass
`use\_profile: true` when you run automation.
> [!NOTE]
>
> This page covers the setup flow. For the exact request/response schema of every profile endpoint, see \*\*Full API Spec\*\* under [TinyAgent Reference](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/tinyagent/api/profiles).
> [card] [TinyProfiles overview](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/key-concepts/tinyprofile.md)
>
> Learn when to use TinyProfile state
> [card] [Vault Credentials](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/key-concepts/credentials.md)
>
> Add stale-session repair
## API setup lifecycle
TinyProfiles are API-controlled saved state. The hosted setup UI is a manual helper; API
users should bring their own Playwright, Puppeteer, or CDP controller and connect to the setup session's
`cdp\_url`. Use `base\_url` only for TinyFish HTTP session endpoints such as `/pages`; do not pass
`base\_url` to Playwright.
\*\*1. Create or list profiles\*\*
Create a named TinyProfile with `POST /v1/profiles`, or list existing profiles and choose one.
\*\*2. Start setup\*\*
Call `POST /v1/profiles/{profileId}/setup-session` and keep the returned `session\_id`,
`cdp\_url`, `base\_url`, `timeout\_seconds`, and `expires\_at`.
\*\*3. Connect and log in\*\*
Connect your browser automation framework to `cdp\_url`, then log in manually or programmatically.
\*\*4. Save or discard\*\*
Save with `POST /v1/profiles/{profileId}/save` and `{ "session\_id": "..." }`. Cancelling
setup or letting it time out discards unsaved setup state.
\*\*5. Run with saved state\*\*
Pass `use\_profile: true`, or pass both `use\_profile: true` and `profile\_id` for a specific
profile.
## Set up a profile
Start a setup browser with `POST /v1/profiles/{profileId}/setup-session` and a target `url`. The
response includes a `cdp\_url` — connect to it with Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, or another CDP
client. For example, with Playwright:
```typescript TypeScript theme={null}
import { chromium } from "playwright";
const CDP\_URL = "";
const browser = await chromium.connectOverCDP(CDP\_URL);
const page = browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0];
await page.goto("https://app.example.com/login");
// Automate the login form here, or use your own CDP tooling to complete login.
```
```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
from playwright.async\_api import async\_playwright
CDP\_URL = ""
async def main():
```

# CartPilot — Store-accurate pricing from the user's postal code

## Context
The user's idea: instead of pricing at T&T's "main" store, use the shopper's address to price at the store they'll actually shop from. Then items are confirmed in stock and prices are accurate.

### Why it matters (live evidence)
- The price search uses TinyFish Fetch, which is anonymous with no cookies. T&T then shows the default postal code **L3T** (seen in the page header), while the signed-in cart is at **N6G**.
- In the build tests, "Burnbrae Farms Large Eggs (12pcs)" was priced and approved but is **not stocked at N6G** (2 of 2 runs). The phase-1 eggs test showed the same thing.
- Each such item wastes agent time (scrolling the results, then "Not at your store") and leaves a gap in the cart.

### Does "postal code → nearest store" work? Yes, in a simpler form
- T&T has no public store picker to match against: `/eng/store-location` is only a "request a store" form.
- T&T's own model is a **postal code in the site header**, and T&T maps that to the fulfilling store itself. So we **set the postal code already saved in the CartPilot profile** (`profile.postalCode`, e.g. "N6G 1A1") and let T&T choose the store. No distance calculation.

### How to set it: a TinyFish remote browser (TinyBrowser)
- `POST https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai` creates a **stealth Chrome session** with `{url, timeout_seconds, proxy_config: {country_code: "CA"}}`, starting in 10–30s. It returns a `cdp_url` for Playwright (`connectOverCDP`). `DELETE /{session_id}` ends it.
- It's driven by **code, not an AI agent**, so each page takes seconds instead of 10–30s agent steps.
- Sessions start anonymous and can't load the saved T&T sign-in. That's fine: an anonymous visitor can set a postal code in the header.

### What it means for speed (honest estimate)
- **Price search:** about the same as now. Session start 10–30s, plus about 3–5s per search page with 3–4 tabs at once, so an 8-item list takes about 30–45s (today's fetch: 30–40s).
- **Cart build:** this is where time is saved. No more agent minutes spent hunting for products that aren't stocked, no "Not at your store" gaps, and fewer retries. Unstocked items are caught on the review screen, where the user can swap them in a second.

## Step 1: Spike (prove it first, ~$0.10, ~10 min)
A throwaway script in the scratchpad, using `playwright-core` (connect-only, no browser download):
1. Create a TinyBrowser session (CA proxy, 120s timeout) on `https://www.tntsupermarket.com/eng/`. **If 404 NOT_FOUND** (TinyBrowser not enabled on the account), stop and use the fallback below.
2. Find the header's postal-code / "Delivery · Pickup" control, enter `N6G 1A1`, and confirm the header shows N6G.
3. Open `search.html?query=large%20eggs` and read the result cards (page `innerText` and product links). **Pass:** the 12-pack eggs that aren't stocked at N6G are missing (compare with the L3T fetch), with no "Access Denied". Also time each step.
4. Close the session.

**Pass → Step 2. Fail → fallback** (in order):
- (a) Run the same postal-code flow through a TinyFish profile setup session (also controllable by code).
- (b) Keep Fetch pricing, and in the review flag items the cart agent previously reported "Not at your store" (cached per postal code), so they show up before approval.

## Step 2: Build it (only if the spike passes)
- **`server/research/storeBrowser.js`**:
  - `createStoreSession({apiKey, postalCode})`: create the session, connect with `playwright-core`, set the postal code with the selectors confirmed in the spike, and check that the header shows it.
  - `fetchPages(urls)` with the **same return shape as `server/research/tinyfish.js`** (`Map<url, {ok, text, links, images}>`). Pages load in 3 tabs at once and wait for the results to render. `text` is the result list's `innerText`; links and images come from the cards.
  - Always deletes the session (`finally`).
- **`server/research/research.js`** needs no change. `researchList` already takes `fetchPages` and runs the parser, matching, fallback searches and totals. `parseSearch` gets fixture tests on browser `innerText` (it already handles one-field-per-line text).
- **`server/index.js`:** the researcher uses `storeBrowser` when `profile.postalCode` is set, and **falls back to Fetch** if the browser fails or isn't enabled (a warning is logged and the result is labelled).
- **Research result:** gains `store: { postalCode, source: "your-store" | "online-catalogue" }`. The `storeNote` text and the review screen say "Prices and stock for N6G" or "Online catalogue prices (set your postal code for store stock)".
- **Profile form:** the postal code hint becomes "Used to price items at your T&T store". If it's empty, the review shows a nudge.
- **Cart agent:** unchanged. Because the review already reflects N6G stock, "Not at your store" should become rare.

## Tests
- `storeBrowser` with a fake CDP/page object: postal code set and verified, tabs limited to 3, session always closed, errors reported per URL.
- `parseSearch` on captured browser `innerText` fixtures.
- Research picks the browser when a postal code is set and falls back to Fetch on failure; `store.source` and labels are correct.
- The existing 76 tests keep passing.

## Verification
1. Spike result: pass/fail, timings, and whether the unstocked eggs disappear at N6G.
2. If built: price the 6-item test list at N6G. The eggs pick should switch to an option that's stocked at N6G. Compare time with Fetch. Then build the cart and check there are no "Not at your store" items.
3. Commit on a new branch stacked on #7 and open a PR with before/after numbers.

# CartPilot — Store-accurate pricing from the user's postal code

## Context
The user's idea: instead of pricing at T&T's "main" store, use the shopper's address to price at the store they'll actually shop from. Then items are confirmed in stock and prices are accurate.

### Why it matters (live evidence)
- The price search uses TinyFish Fetch, which is anonymous with no cookies. T&T then shows the default postal code **L3T** (seen in the page header), while the signed-in cart is at **N6G**.
- In the build tests, "Burnbrae Farms Large Eggs (12pcs)" was priced and approved but is **not stocked at N6G** (2 of 2 runs). The phase-1 eggs test showed the same thing.
- Each such item wastes agent time (scrolling the results, then "Not at your store") and leaves a gap in the cart.

### Does "postal code → nearest store" work? Yes, in a simpler form
- T&T has no public store picker to match against: `/eng/store-location` is only a "request a store" form.
- T&T's own model is a **postal code in the site header**, and T&T maps that to the fulfilling store itself. So we **set the postal code already saved in the CartPilot profile** (`profile.postalCode`, e.g. "N6G 1A1") and let T&T choose the store. No distance calculation.

### How to set it: a TinyFish remote browser (TinyBrowser)
- `POST https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai` creates a **stealth Chrome session** with `{url, timeout_seconds, proxy_config: {country_code: "CA"}}`, starting in 10–30s. It returns a `cdp_url` for Playwright (`connectOverCDP`). `DELETE /{session_id}` ends it.
- It's driven by **code, not an AI agent**, so each page takes seconds instead of 10–30s agent steps.
- Sessions start anonymous and can't load the saved T&T sign-in. That's fine: an anonymous visitor can set a postal code in the header.

### What it means for speed (honest estimate)
- **Price search:** about the same as now. Session start 10–30s, plus about 3–5s per search page with 3–4 tabs at once, so an 8-item list takes about 30–45s (today's fetch: 30–40s).
- **Cart build:** this is where time is saved. No more agent minutes spent hunting for products that aren't stocked, no "Not at your store" gaps, and fewer retries. Unstocked items are caught on the review screen, where the user can swap them in a second.

## Step 1: Spike (prove it first, ~$0.10, ~10 min)
A throwaway script in the scratchpad, using `playwright-core` (connect-only, no browser download):
1. Create a TinyBrowser session (CA proxy, 120s timeout) on `https://www.tntsupermarket.com/eng/`. **If 404 NOT_FOUND** (TinyBrowser not enabled on the account), stop and use the fallback below.
2. Find the header's postal-code / "Delivery · Pickup" control, enter `N6G 1A1`, and confirm the header shows N6G.
3. Open `search.html?query=large%20eggs` and read the result cards (page `innerText` and product links). **Pass:** the 12-pack eggs that aren't stocked at N6G are missing (compare with the L3T fetch), with no "Access Denied". Also time each step.
4. Close the session.

**Pass → Step 2. Fail → fallback** (in order):
- (a) Run the same postal-code flow through a TinyFish profile setup session (also controllable by code).
- (b) Keep Fetch pricing, and in the review flag items the cart agent previously reported "Not at your store" (cached per postal code), so they show up before approval.

## Step 2: Build it (only if the spike passes)
- **`server/research/storeBrowser.js`**:
  - `createStoreSession({apiKey, postalCode})`: create the session, connect with `playwright-core`, set the postal code with the selectors confirmed in the spike, and check that the header shows it.
  - `fetchPages(urls)` with the **same return shape as `server/research/tinyfish.js`** (`Map<url, {ok, text, links, images}>`). Pages load in 3 tabs at once and wait for the results to render. `text` is the result list's `innerText`; links and images come from the cards.
  - Always deletes the session (`finally`).
- **`server/research/research.js`** needs no change. `researchList` already takes `fetchPages` and runs the parser, matching, fallback searches and totals. `parseSearch` gets fixture tests on browser `innerText` (it already handles one-field-per-line text).
- **`server/index.js`:** the researcher uses `storeBrowser` when `profile.postalCode` is set, and **falls back to Fetch** if the browser fails or isn't enabled (a warning is logged and the result is labelled).
- **Research result:** gains `store: { postalCode, source: "your-store" | "online-catalogue" }`. The `storeNote` text and the review screen say "Prices and stock for N6G" or "Online catalogue prices (set your postal code for store stock)".
- **Profile form:** the postal code hint becomes "Used to price items at your T&T store". If it's empty, the review shows a nudge.
- **Cart agent:** unchanged. Because the review already reflects N6G stock, "Not at your store" should become rare.

## Tests
- `storeBrowser` with a fake CDP/page object: postal code set and verified, tabs limited to 3, session always closed, errors reported per URL.
- `parseSearch` on captured browser `innerText` fixtures.
- Research picks the browser when a postal code is set and falls back to Fetch on failure; `store.source` and labels are correct.
- The existing 76 tests keep passing.

## Verification
1. Spike result: pass/fail, timings, and whether the unstocked eggs disappear at N6G.
2. If built: price the 6-item test list at N6G. The eggs pick should switch to an option that's stocked at N6G. Compare time with Fetch. Then build the cart and check there are no "Not at your store" items.
3. Commit on a new branch stacked on #7 and open a PR with before/after numbers.

> Stacked on #7. Merge #6 → #7 → this one; retarget each to `main` as the previous one merges.

## Why
Prices come from T&T's online catalogue, because TinyFish Fetch can't pick a store. The cart agent, though, shops signed in at the user's store (N6G). Some products priced and approved weren't found there ("Not at your store"), which wastes agent time and leaves gaps in the cart.

## First: can we price the user's store directly? (spike, ~12 short TinyFish browser sessions)
| Finding | |
|---|---|
| TinyFish remote browser (TinyBrowser) on T&T | ✅ starts in under 1s, T&T loads in ~10s, no "Access Denied" |
| How T&T picks the store | It stores `x-postcode` and `x-prefered-store-code` in browser storage (e.g. L3T → `UV`) and sends both with every product search (`ProductSearch` request headers) |
| Set the postal code ourselves | ✅ the header switches to N6G |
| Get the store code for a postal code | ❌ Only T&T's pickup dialog does this, and it needs a Google Map that doesn't render in the remote browser. Magento's `pickupLocations` query is disabled ("Something went wrong"), and the saved profile doesn't keep the store choice. Without the code, T&T falls back to store `WS` and results don't change. |

So direct pricing needs T&T's postal-code-to-store mapping, which is recorded in the README as future work.

## What this PR does instead: learn stock from the cart agent
- **`store_stock` table:** per postal area (FSA, e.g. `N6G`) and product URL, it records available / out of stock / not found. These are store facts only, nothing personal, kept for 14 days.
  - "Out of stock" counts straight away.
  - "Not found" needs **two** misses, because agents sometimes miss a card (we saw garlic missed once and then found).
  - "Added" clears the record.
- **Recorded:** after every cart build.
- **Used** in the price search and "Search again" (`applyStoreStock`):
  - a product the store didn't have is **swapped** for an alternative it did have (or one with no record yet);
  - if there's no other option, it's **flagged** on the review screen;
  - totals and warnings are updated.
- **Review screen:** explains swaps and flags, and how many products' stock is known for the user's store.

## Tests
- [x] `npm test`: 82 pass (6 new)
  - postal area parsing;
  - no record means no change;
  - swap preference (seen in stock → no record);
  - flag when no option is left;
  - the two-miss rule, "added" clearing it, stores kept separate;
  - **end to end:** a build reports out of stock → the next price search swaps the item.
- [ ] Manual: build a cart where something is "Not at your store", then re-price and see the swap

EOF

content.text:
Your idea is right in principle, and T&T works almost exactly that way, but I couldn't get it working automatically. So I built a workaround that gets most of the benefit. It's in **PR #8: https://github.com/GLeanM/HackWestern13/pull/8**, built on #7, and all 82 tests pass.

## What I found (about a dozen short test sessions, a few cents)
- **T&T already maps a postal code to a store.** Your browser keeps two values: your postal code (anonymous visitors get L3T) and a store code (L3T → store "UV"). Every product search sends both, and the results depend on the store code. So "postal code → nearest store" is how T&T itself works, and you never need to choose a store yourself.
- **TinyFish's remote browser works on T&T:** it starts in under a second, loads T&T in about 10 seconds, and wasn't blocked. CartPilot can set your postal code (the header switched to N6G).
- **The blocker:** T&T only works out the store code inside its pickup dialog, and that dialog needs a Google Map that doesn't load in the remote browser. I tried three ways around it, and none worked:
  - Magento's standard store-lookup query is switched off.
  - Your saved TinyFish profile doesn't keep the store choice.
  - With only the postal code set, T&T fell back to some other store ("WS") and showed the same results.
- **So prices from your actual store aren't possible yet.** It would work if we knew London's store code; finding that automatically is listed as future work in the README.

## The workaround: CartPilot learns your store from the cart agent
The cart agent shops signed in at your N6G store, so it already knows what's there. Now:
- **Every cart build records what happened at your store,** by postal area (N6G): added means in stock, and "not at your store" or out of stock means missing.
- **The next price search uses that:** a product your store didn't have is swapped for an option it did have, or flagged on the review screen before you approve. You see something like "Switched automatically: the first choice wasn't stocked at your T&T store last time."
- **It's careful about agent mistakes.** "Couldn't find it" has to happen **twice** before it counts, because we saw an agent miss garlic once and find it the next time. Out of stock counts straight away, and a later successful add clears the record.
- **It only stores store facts** (postal area + product), nothing about you, and they expire after 14 days.

## Will it make CartPilot faster?
Yes, a little, but it's mainly an accuracy fix:
- **Price search:** no faster (still about 30–40s).
- **Cart build:** quicker over time. Each unstocked item used to cost an agent a minute or more of scrolling before "Not at your store"; now those get avoided before the agent starts.
- **Start-up:** it learns from your first build, so the first one won't benefit yet.

**An honest caveat:** I'm now less sure the eggs were really unstocked at your store. They showed up in every anonymous search, so some of the earlier "Not at your store" results may have been the agent missing the card. The twice-before-it-counts rule covers this.

## Merge order and next steps
- **Merge in order:** #6 → #7 → #8, changing each PR's base to `main` as the one before it merges.
- **To see it working:** do a full build, then click **Refresh T&T prices**. Anything the agent couldn't get should now be swapped or flagged.

input.content:
# Autocart: UI/UX redesign

## Context
The app works end to end, but the UI is one long, plain page. The user asked for:
1. A **white and green** colour scheme that matches T&T.
2. A rename from CartPilot to **Autocart** (a play on Instacart).
3. The **live browser agent shown inside the build-cart section**. Today `CartBuild` renders above the review list and `ApproveCart` below it (`src/PlanPanel.jsx`).
4. A **shopping list that fills in prices as it appears**. Today pricing waits for a separate "Find prices on T&T" click.
5. A layout that **feels like a web app**.

Branch: `autocart-redesign`, created from `phase-6d-store-stock` (stacked on PR #8).

## Information architecture: 4 steps in an app shell
```
┌ Top bar: [cart logo] Autocart ············ budget pill · avatar ▾ (log out) ┐
├ Sidebar (desktop) ─┬ Main (one step at a time) ──────┬ Summary rail (≥1200px) ┤
│ 1 Profile      ✓   │                                 │ Budget meter           │
│ 2 Meal plan    ✓   │                                 │ Total · items          │
│ 3 Cart         ●   │                                 │ Next action button     │
│ 4 Build cart   🔒   │                                 │                        │
└────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘
Mobile: steps become a horizontal pill bar under the top bar; the summary becomes a sticky bottom bar.
```
- **1 Profile:** the existing `ProfileForm`, regrouped into cards (Budget & household · Food preferences · Pantry · Store postal code). Saving moves on to step 2.
- **2 Meal plan:** the note box and **"Plan & price my groceries"** (one button). While planning, skeleton cards show; then the summary, the meal plan by day (grid of day cards), pantry-covered chips and warnings.
- **3 Cart (the list and prices together):** once the plan is ready, the list shows **straight away**, grouped by category, with each row showing a "Finding T&T price…" shimmer. Prices fill in when research finishes, and the rows then become the editable review rows (swap / packs / remove / search again: today's `ReviewCart`). The summary rail updates live.
- **4 Build cart:** the approval card (`ApproveCart`) → after approval, in the **same section**: the **large live TinyFish browser view(s)**, the agent's current action, Stop, per-item outcomes, then "Open my T&T cart".
- **Navigation:** the step a task is on is opened automatically (`planning`/`planned` → 2, `researching`/`priced` → 3, `building`/`built` → 4). The user can go back to earlier steps; later steps stay locked until they're reached.

## Plan and price in one go (server)
- `startPlanningTask` (`server/tasks.js`) gets `autoPrice` + `researcher`. When planning succeeds and the list isn't empty:
  - `db.claimResearch`;
  - `startResearchTask` (existing; it already applies store stock);
  - the status moves `planning → planned → researching → priced` with no extra click.
- `createApp` gets an `autoPrice` option (default `true`) passed through the `POST /shopping-tasks` route. Existing tests set `autoPrice: false`; a new test proves the chaining.
- "Refresh T&T prices" stays (step 3 overflow menu).

## Visual system (`src/styles.css`, rewritten with tokens)
- **Light, white-and-green theme:**
  - background `#F6F8F6`, cards white;
  - brand green `#00843D` (T&T-like), deep green `#0B4F2E` for headings and the active nav item, mint tint `#E8F5EC` for selected and active states;
  - text `#17211B`, muted `#5D6B62`, borders `#E1E7E2`;
  - danger `#C62828`, warning `#B26A00`.
- Inter (Google Fonts in `index.html`). 8px spacing scale, 12px card radius, soft shadows, focus rings, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected.
- **Shared components** (`src/ui.jsx`): `Button` (primary / secondary / ghost / danger), `Card`, `Chip`, `Skeleton`, `Stepper`, `BudgetMeter`, and small inline SVG icons (cart, check, lock, leaf, spark, stop).
- The layout works at 360px with no sideways scrolling.

## Rename to Autocart
- `index.html` `<title>Autocart</title>`, the top-bar logo/wordmark, the login landing page, the footer ("Not affiliated with T&T Supermarket. Autocart never places orders or pays.").
- UI copy saying "CartPilot" → "Autocart" (`ApproveCart`, `CartBuild`, `ReviewCart`, `ProfileForm`).
- `package.json` name → `autocart`. TinyFish `api_integration: "autocart"`. README title, tagline and text. The Auth0 API identifier stays `https://cartpilot-api` (renaming it would break login); the README notes this.

## Login landing page
A white hero with a green gradient band: "Autocart: your grocery cart, built for you", 3 feature tiles (Plan meals · Price at T&T · Agent fills your cart), and Log in / Sign up buttons.

## Files
- **New:** `src/ui.jsx` (shared components + icons), `src/AppShell.jsx` (top bar, sidebar steps, summary rail, mobile pill bar), `src/steps/MealPlanStep.jsx`, `src/steps/CartStep.jsx`, `src/steps/BuildStep.jsx`, `src/Landing.jsx`.
- **Reworked:**
  - `src/App.jsx` becomes the shell plus the step router; task loading and polling move here from `PlanPanel`.
  - `src/PlanPanel.jsx` is replaced by the step components.
  - `ReviewCart.jsx` gets shimmer rows while pricing.
  - `ApproveCart.jsx` and `CartBuild.jsx` are restyled and placed in `BuildStep`.
  - `ProfileForm.jsx` is regrouped.
- **Server:** `server/tasks.js`, `server/app.js` (+ tests).
- **Dev-only preview:** `src/preview.html` + `src/Preview.jsx`, served by Vite in dev only. They render every step with sample data (planning, pricing shimmer, priced, building with a fake live view, built) so the design can be checked and screenshotted without signing in.

## Verification
1. Run `npm test`: all pass, plus the new auto-pricing test.
2. Run `npx vite build`: succeeds.
3. Open the dev preview in the browser (Claude in Chrome) at desktop and 375px widths and screenshot each step state: correct colours, no overflow, the agent view sitting inside Build cart.
4. Smoke test against the real API: the routes are unchanged apart from the auto-pricing chain, so `POST /shopping-tasks` ends at `priced` with a real login (the user checks this in the browser).
5. Commit on `autocart-redesign` and open a PR stacked on #8 with screenshots.

2. A rename from CartPilot to **Autocart** (a play on Instacart).
3. The **live browser agent shown inside the build-cart section**. Today `CartBuild` renders above the review list and `ApproveCart` below it (`src/PlanPanel.jsx`).
4. A **shopping list that fills in prices as it appears**. Today pricing waits for a separate "Find prices on T&T" click.
5. A layout that **feels like a web app**.

Branch: `autocart-redesign`, created from `phase-6d-store-stock` (stacked on PR #8).

## Information architecture: 4 steps in an app shell
```
┌ Top bar: [cart logo] Autocart ············ budget pill · avatar ▾ (log out) ┐

│ 4 Build cart   🔒   │                                 │                        │
└────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘
Mobile: steps become a horizontal pill bar under the top bar; the summary becomes a sticky bottom bar.
```
- **1 Profile:** the existing `ProfileForm`, regrouped into cards (Budget & household · Food preferences · Pantry · Store postal code). Saving moves on to step 2.
- **2 Meal plan:** the note box and **"Plan & price my groceries"** (one button). While planning, skeleton cards show; then the summary, the meal plan by day (grid of day cards), pantry-covered chips and warnings.

Prices fill in when research finishes, and the rows then become the editable review rows (swap / packs / remove / search again: today's `ReviewCart`). The summary rail updates live.
- **4 Build cart:** the approval card (`ApproveCart`) → after approval, in the **same section**: the **large live TinyFish browser view(s)**, the agent's current action, Stop, per-item outcomes, then "Open my T&T cart".

## Plan and price in one go (server)
- `startPlanningTask` (`server/tasks.js`) gets `autoPrice` + `researcher`. When planning succeeds and the list isn't empty:

  - `src/App.jsx` becomes the shell plus the step router; task loading and polling move here from `PlanPanel`.
  - `src/PlanPanel.jsx` is replaced by the step components.
  - `ReviewCart.jsx` gets shimmer rows while pricing.
  - `ApproveCart.jsx` and `CartBuild.jsx` are restyled and placed in `BuildStep`.
  - `ProfileForm.jsx` is regrouped.
- **Server:** `server/tasks.js`, `server/app.js` (+ tests).
- **Dev-only preview:** `src/preview.html` + `src/Preview.jsx`, served by Vite in dev only. They render every step with sample data (planning, pricing shimmer, priced, building with a fake live view, built) so the design can be checked and screenshotted without signing in.

# CartPilot — Store-accurate pricing from the user's postal code

## Context
The user's idea: instead of pricing at T&T's "main" store, use the shopper's address to price at the store they'll actually shop from. Then items are confirmed in stock and prices are accurate.

### Why it matters (live evidence)
- The price search uses TinyFish Fetch, which is anonymous with no cookies. T&T then shows the default postal code **L3T** (seen in the page header), while the signed-in cart is at **N6G**.
- In the build tests, "Burnbrae Farms Large Eggs (12pcs)" was priced and approved but is **not stocked at N6G** (2 of 2 runs). The phase-1 eggs test showed the same thing.
- Each such item wastes agent time (scrolling the results, then "Not at your store") and leaves a gap in the cart.

### Does "postal code → nearest store" work? Yes, in a simpler form
- T&T has no public store picker to match against: `/eng/store-location` is only a "request a store" form.
- T&T's own model is a **postal code in the site header**, and T&T maps that to the fulfilling store itself. So we **set the postal code already saved in the CartPilot profile** (`profile.postalCode`, e.g. "N6G 1A1") and let T&T choose the store. No distance calculation.

### How to set it: a TinyFish remote browser (TinyBrowser)
- `POST https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai` creates a **stealth Chrome session** with `{url, timeout_seconds, proxy_config: {country_code: "CA"}}`, starting in 10–30s. It returns a `cdp_url` for Playwright (`connectOverCDP`). `DELETE /{session_id}` ends it.
- It's driven by **code, not an AI agent**, so each page takes seconds instead of 10–30s agent steps.
- Sessions start anonymous and can't load the saved T&T sign-in. That's fine: an anonymous visitor can set a postal code in the header.

### What it means for speed (honest estimate)
- **Price search:** about the same as now. Session start 10–30s, plus about 3–5s per search page with 3–4 tabs at once, so an 8-item list takes about 30–45s (today's fetch: 30–40s).
- **Cart build:** this is where time is saved. No more agent minutes spent hunting for products that aren't stocked, no "Not at your store" gaps, and fewer retries. Unstocked items are caught on the review screen, where the user can swap them in a second.

## Step 1: Spike (prove it first, ~$0.10, ~10 min)
A throwaway script in the scratchpad, using `playwright-core` (connect-only, no browser download):
1. Create a TinyBrowser session (CA proxy, 120s timeout) on `https://www.tntsupermarket.com/eng/`. **If 404 NOT_FOUND** (TinyBrowser not enabled on the account), stop and use the fallback below.
2. Find the header's postal-code / "Delivery · Pickup" control, enter `N6G 1A1`, and confirm the header shows N6G.
3. Open `search.html?query=large%20eggs` and read the result cards (page `innerText` and product links). **Pass:** the 12-pack eggs that aren't stocked at N6G are missing (compare with the L3T fetch), with no "Access Denied". Also time each step.
4. Close the session.

**Pass → Step 2. Fail → fallback** (in order):
- (a) Run the same postal-code flow through a TinyFish profile setup session (also controllable by code).
- (b) Keep Fetch pricing, and in the review flag items the cart agent previously reported "Not at your store" (cached per postal code), so they show up before approval.

## Step 2: Build it (only if the spike passes)
- **`server/research/storeBrowser.js`**:
  - `createStoreSession({apiKey, postalCode})`: create the session, connect with `playwright-core`, set the postal code with the selectors confirmed in the spike, and check that the header shows it.
  - `fetchPages(urls)` with the **same return shape as `server/research/tinyfish.js`** (`Map<url, {ok, text, links, images}>`). Pages load in 3 tabs at once and wait for the results to render. `text` is the result list's `innerText`; links and images come from the cards.
  - Always deletes the session (`finally`).
- **`server/research/research.js`** needs no change. `researchList` already takes `fetchPages` and runs the parser, matching, fallback searches and totals. `parseSearch` gets fixture tests on browser `innerText` (it already handles one-field-per-line text).
- **`server/index.js`:** the researcher uses `storeBrowser` when `profile.postalCode` is set, and **falls back to Fetch** if the browser fails or isn't enabled (a warning is logged and the result is labelled).
- **Research result:** gains `store: { postalCode, source: "your-store" | "online-catalogue" }`. The `storeNote` text and the review screen say "Prices and stock for N6G" or "Online catalogue prices (set your postal code for store stock)".
- **Profile form:** the postal code hint becomes "Used to price items at your T&T store". If it's empty, the review shows a nudge.
- **Cart agent:** unchanged. Because the review already reflects N6G stock, "Not at your store" should become rare.

## Tests
- `storeBrowser` with a fake CDP/page object: postal code set and verified, tabs limited to 3, session always closed, errors reported per URL.
- `parseSearch` on captured browser `innerText` fixtures.
- Research picks the browser when a postal code is set and falls back to Fetch on failure; `store.source` and labels are correct.
- The existing 76 tests keep passing.

## Verification
1. Spike result: pass/fail, timings, and whether the unstocked eggs disappear at N6G.
2. If built: price the 6-item test list at N6G. The eggs pick should switch to an option that's stocked at N6G. Compare time with Fetch. Then build the cart and check there are no "Not at your store" items.
3. Commit on a new branch stacked on #7 and open a PR with before/after numbers.

content.text:
# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

# Autocart

**Your grocery cart, built for you.** (A play on Instacart.) HackWestern 2026, built for the Auth0 and TinyFish sponsor tracks.

You give Autocart a grocery budget, household size, food preferences, things to avoid, and what's already in your pantry. 2. **Profile.** Budget, people, days, diet, cuisines, allergies, foods to skip, nutrition and cooking preferences, postal code, and pantry. Saved per user.
3. **Plan.** Google Gemini (structured JSON output) produces a structured meal plan and ingredient list. Server code (not the LLM) merges duplicates, removes pantry items and exclusions.

4. **Research.** TinyFish Fetch reads T&T's search page for every item at once (about 30–40s for a full list). Server code parses the results, screens out allergens and "different foods" (quail eggs aren't eggs), picks the cheapest pack that covers the recipe quantity, retries simpler searches when nothing matches, and totals the cart against the budget.

| POST | `/api/shopping-tasks/:id/research` | `read:profile` | Look up every list item on T&T and price it (read-only; nothing is added to a cart). Returns `202` with status `researching`, then `priced`. Re-pricing keeps review choices where possible |

- T&T's website answers "Access Denied" to automated **direct product-page links** and to **two agents on one account at once**, while its search pages keep working. The agent therefore uses TinyFish's stealth browser, starts at the home page, adds items from search results, and runs one at a time. On the same items this went from ~27 minutes / 222 steps with mostly failures to ~3 minutes / 19 steps with everything added.

- Going straight to `search.html?query=…` instead of typing in the search box cut each item from 4–9 agent steps to 2–3 (the box only shows a suggestion dropdown first). The best runs add an item in ~30s.

-- What's left of the time is outside CartPilot: ~35s for TinyFish to start each browser, 8–35s per agent step depending on the session, slow-loading T&T pages, and a subscription popup. Two agents at once hide a slow session behind a fast one; T&T didn't block this with search pages.

+- What's left of the time is outside Autocart: ~35s for TinyFish to start each browser, 8–35s per agent step depending on the session, slow-loading T&T pages, and a subscription popup. Two agents at once hide a slow session behind a fast one; T&T didn't block this with search pages.
- T&T's cart counts weight items in pounds, so the agent gets a pound target (e.g. "about 2 lb") and never reduces an existing amount; it used to cut 2 lb of pork to "1".

-- Prices come from T&T's online catalogue (default store), but the signed-in store may not stock every item ("Not at your store"). CartPilot now **learns each store's stock from the cart agent**: what it adds or finds out of stock is recorded per postal area (FSA, e.g. N6G). On the next price search, products that store didn't have are swapped for an option it did have, or flagged on the review screen before you approve. A single "couldn't find it" needs to happen twice before it counts, because agents occasionally miss a card.

Autocart now **learns each store's stock from the cart agent**: what it adds or finds out of stock is recorded per postal area (FSA, e.g. N6G). On the next price search, products that store didn't have are swapped for an option it did have, or flagged on the review screen before you approve. A single "couldn't find it" needs to happen twice before it counts, because agents occasionally miss a card.

- **Why not price the user's store directly?** We tested it. T&T keeps the shopper's postal code and store code in browser storage (`x-postcode`, `x-prefered-store-code`) and sends both with every product search. A TinyFish remote browser can set the postal code, but T&T only maps a postal code to a store inside its pickup dialog, which needs a Google Map that doesn't load in the remote browser. Magento's standard `pickupLocations` query is disabled, and the saved TinyFish profile doesn't keep the store choice. With the right store code this would work; finding it automatically is future work.
- A blocked agent used to keep trying for 100+ steps; it now stops at the first block and reports it as **blocked** (not "out of stock").
- If the server restarts mid-build, leftover TinyFish runs are cancelled on startup so they don't keep costing money.
